unclassified.doc:
The curated set: seeds found by `npm run find:highballs`, each proven to go
by the solver at test time (`highball.test.ts`), graded by the assessment.

The route book.
Routes are plain data. Nothing in the sim knows any of these exist, and
adding a hundred more means adding a hundred more entries here — no game
code changes. Ids are stable because scores, projects and betas are stored
against them.

The top of the board, V11 to V17. Nobody hand-sets a route seven metres
up the cave hold by hold; these were set by the route setter, climbed
by the same headless climber, and pinned here by their generator ids, so
they rebuild exactly from the id and never need climbing again at load.
Unlike the setter's corner, they are board routes: they count toward your
grade.
Decorative off-route holds. Rendered dim grey, never grabbable.

The shape table. Nothing here is exposed to the player as numbers — the
inspect panel shows the label and the note, and the rest is learned by
getting spat off a sloper you approached from the wrong angle.
The holds on the title wall: a few problems' worth of tape colours.

characters.name: Chad
characters.desc: This one's pretty soft. Has never once graded a route correctly. Sets big moves off good holds and is baffled when people fall.

characters.name: Melissa
characters.desc: It goes. You have to want it. Technical to the point of cruelty. Every hold works, from exactly one position.

characters.name: Dyno Dave
characters.desc: Just jump, man. Believes every problem is a jumping problem. Is correct more often than anyone would like.

characters.name: Kevin
characters.desc: I found some new volumes. Uses fourteen volumes. Has been asked to stop. Has not stopped.

characters.name: The Sadist
characters.desc: Everything you need is on the wall. Technically fair. Emotionally unacceptable.

characters.name: The Gym
characters.desc: Warm up properly. Set by whoever was on shift. Honest, unglamorous, does the job.

proposals.label: A · Conservative
proposals.proposal: Give Chad, Melissa and Dyno Dave a voice: one line each where the player meets them, one more later.
changes: Write 2 lines per character tied to existing missions or places.
Have each say something only they would say (their job, their worry).
proposals.experience: Names become people; players start to recognise them.

validation.metric: characters with ≥ 2 mentions and a line
validation.method: STORYCRAFT re-run; playtest: name three characters.

proposals.existing: Chad, Melissa, Dyno Dave, Kevin and 2 more are defined as characters but appear in at most one authored line and never speak.
proposals.problem: 6 named characters are barely present in the writing
proposals.why: A named character the player meets once is set dressing with a name tag. Each one is an unpaid promise of a relationship.

proposals.label: B · Ambitious
proposals.proposal: Build a small arc around one of them (Chad).
changes: Three beats across the campaign: Chad asks, Chad is in trouble, Chad pays it back.
Attach each beat to a mission the player already plays.
proposals.experience: A relationship that develops over hours; the payoff lands because the player was there for the setup.

validation.method: STORYCRAFT re-run; playtest emotional rating at the payoff.

proposals.label: C · Wild card
proposals.proposal: Make The Gym unreliable: what they say early turns out to be false.
changes: Plant a claim; let a later mission reveal the truth.
proposals.experience: Players reread the world; characters gain depth through contradiction.
proposals.complexity_why: a planted line and a reveal
tradeoffs: Risk of feeling like a cheap twist.
